reason: The hypothesis directly combines the specific finding that reducing Ti content promotes CrTaO4 formation (P1, P8) with the finding that ultrafine grain refinement enhances chromia/alumina scale formation (P5, P21, P26) into a single proposal. However, P1 already explicitly states that reduced Ti content promoted the CrTaO4 layer, and P5 already demonstrates that grain refinement improves oxidation resistance via enhanced diffusion and protective scale formation. The hypothesis merely juxtaposes these two known strategies without a new mechanistic link or transfer to a novel alloy system; it restates their individual conclusions as a combined prediction.
copied_elements: Reducing Ti content to promote protective oxide (P1, P8)
Ultrafine grain refinement via stationary friction processing (P5, P26)
Grain boundaries enhance diffusion of Cr and Al (P19, P21, P26)
Formation of continuous Cr2O3/Al2O3 protective layer (P5, P21, P26)
Lower mass gain and slower oxidation kinetics (P5, P11, P21, P26)
Baseline with coarse grains and higher reactive elements (P1, P5)
